message.content:
In Texas, tenants have a number of statutory rights designed to protect them from unfair treatment and ensure safe, habitable living conditions. Below is an overview of key tenant rights under Texas law (Texas Property Code, Chapter 24) and related statutes: | Category | Key Rights | Practical Implications | |----------|------------|------------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to one month’s rent for a furnished unit and two months’ rent for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within 30 days after lease ends, minus deductions for damages beyond normal wear & tear. | • Keep records of move‑in condition (photos, inventory list).
• Request a written itemized statement if you believe deductions are unjustified. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity, and pest control.
• Must keep the premises in a safe, sanitary condition. | • Report problems promptly in writing.
• If landlord fails to fix, you may withhold rent, repair & deduct, or terminate the lease (see below). | | **Repair & Deduct / Withhold Rent** | • If landlord fails to repair within a reasonable time after notice, tenant may:
 1. Pay for repairs and deduct cost from rent (up to $500).
 2. Withhold rent until repairs are made (up to $500).
 3. Terminate lease if repairs are not made within 30 days. | • Document all communications and keep receipts. | | **Notice Requirements** | • For non‑payment of rent: 3‑day notice to pay or vacate.
• For lease termination: 30‑day notice for month‑to‑month agreements; 60‑day for longer leases.
• For entry: 48‑hour written notice for non‑emergency visits. | • Keep copies of all notices sent/received. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord cannot disturb your peaceful use of the property. | • If landlord repeatedly enters without proper notice, you may sue for damages. | | **Anti‑Discrimination** | • Protected classes: race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, etc. | • Landlords cannot refuse to rent or impose different terms based on protected characteristics. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must file a complaint in district court and serve a summons.
• Tenant has 5 days to respond.
• Court will schedule a hearing; if found liable, a writ of possession is issued. | • Attend the hearing; bring evidence of payment, repair requests, or other defenses. | | **Lease Terms** | • Lease must be in writing if it lasts longer than one year.
• Landlord cannot add new terms after signing unless both parties agree. | • Read the lease carefully before signing; negotiate terms if needed. | | **Rent Control** | • Texas does not have statewide rent control; landlords set rent freely. | • However, rent increases must comply with notice requirements (usually 30 days). | | **Subletting / Assignment** | • Landlord may prohibit subletting only if it is clearly stated in the lease. | • If prohibited, violating this clause can lead to lease termination. | | **Utilities** | • Landlord must provide hot water, electricity, and gas. | • If utilities fail, you may withhold rent or repair & deduct. | | **Landlord’s Right to Enter** | • Must give 48‑hour written notice except in emergencies. | • Keep a log of entries; if unauthorized, you may sue for damages. | ### How to Protect Your Rights 1. **Document Everything** – Photos, videos, written communication, and receipts help prove your case. 2. **Know the Timeline** – Understand how many days you have to respond to notices or to repair issues. 3. **Use Written Notices** – Send all notices via certified mail or email with read receipt. 4. **Seek Legal Advice** – If disputes arise, consult a lawyer or tenant advocacy group (e.g., Texas Tenants Union). 5. **File Complaints** – If landlord violates habitability standards, report to the local health department or the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs. ### Resources - **Texas Property Code** – Chapter 24 (Residential Landlord‑Tenant Law) - **Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection Division** – Provides consumer guides on landlord‑tenant issues. - **Local Housing Authorities** – Offer mediation services and legal aid. - **Legal Aid Organizations** – e.g., Texas Legal Services Center, local bar association referral programs. --- If you’re facing a specific issue (e.g., eviction notice, maintenance dispute), let me know the details and I can help draft a formal letter or outline next steps.
